title: Kalaupapa transition to Maui County under Act 171
summary: Act 171 has Maui County take over the area one year after the last patient leaves, and the state Department of Health said it will wind down regardless; only four patients remain on the registry. Homestead groups opposed or urged a pause, the managing director doubted there would be no county costs, and the item was deferred with Department of Hawaiian Home Lands (DHHL) beneficiary consultations expected in early 2027.

timeline.text: Defer the item on transitioning the county to Maui County: No one objected, so the item was deferred.
The chair said Molokaʻi Community Plan changes would come after the last patient, going to the council and the Molokaʻi Planning Commission.
A resource person said a past Department of Hawaiian Home Lands (DHHL) beneficiary working group agreed homesteading would not be part of Kalaupapa.
The chair said the state asked Maui County to step in because no local government would remain.
The state's aquatic resources division plans to write place-based rules for the peninsula but has not started.
Department of Hawaiian Home Lands (DHHL) expects the first of three beneficiary consultation meetings in February or March 2027.
The chair formed a community advisory group, or hui, which has met three times.
The law starts after the last patient leaves; one year later, Maui County takes over the area.
The chair said Senate Bill 1432 became Act 171 on June 26, 2026.
